questions.question: The currency convertibility concept in its original form is originated in ________.
questions.solution: The Bretton Woods Agreement is the landmark system for monetary and exchange rate management established in 1944. It was developed at the United Nations Monetary and Financial Conference held in Bretton Woods, New Hampshire, from July 1 to July 22, 1944. Under the agreement, currencies were pegged to the price of gold, and the U.S. dollar was seen as a reserve currency linked to the price of gold.

questions.question: India has changed over to the decimal system of coinage in ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**April, 1957**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• India change the decimal system of coinage in April 1957.

 
 
• In 1957, India shifted to the decimal system, but for a short period, both decimal and non-decimal coins were in circulation.
 
• To distinguish between the two, the coins minted between 1957 and 1964 have the legend “Naya Paisa” (“new” paisa).
 
• The denominations in circulation were 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 25, 50 paise, and 1 rupee.

questions.question: Which of the following Vedic texts mentioned the eastern and western seas for the first time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Satpath Brahmana.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A commentary on the **sukla (white) Yajurveda** is found in the** Satpath Brahmana.**
 
• It is credited to** Yajnavalkya, a Vedic guru.**
 
• It is said to be the most **comprehensive, organized, and significant** of the Brahmanas.
 
• It includes thorough **explanations of Vedic mythology, symbolism, and sacrifice **procedures.
 
• As the source of various **Puranic stories and the incarnations of the RigVedic god Vishnu**, the Shatapatha Brahmana is also seen as important in establishing** Vaishnavism.**
 
• This Vedic texts mentioned the **eastern and western seas** for the first time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tandya Brahmana:**

 
 
• It is a **Samaveda Brahmana **that is a part of both the **Kauthuma and Ranayaniya shakhas.**
 
 
 
• **Gopath Brahmana:**
 
 
• **​**The only Brahmana related with the **Atharvaveda **is the Gopatha Brahmana, a category of **prose books outlining Vedic ceremonies.**
 
 
 
• **Kaustiki Brahmana:**
 
 
• **​**An old Sanskrit work called the** Kaushitaki Upanishad is part of the Rigveda. **

questions.question: Mir Hassan Dehlavi was in the court of which of the following?
questions.solution:

questions.question: Which of the following planets has the highest rotational motion?
questions.solution:
• Jupiter is the fifth planet from the Sun and the largest in the Solar System.
 
• It is a giant planet with a mass one-thousandth that of the Sun, but two-and-a-half times that of all the other planets in the Solar System combined.
 
• Jupiter is the fastest spinning planet about its axis.
 
• It completes one rotation about its axis in about 10 hrs whereas Earth takes about 24 hours.

questions.question: If any Fundamental Right of a citizen is breached then under Article 226 of Indian Constitution he can move to ________.
questions.solution:
Option **4** is correct, i.e. __**High Court of State**__.

__
 
• Under **Article 226**, a writ petition can be filed in a **High court__ for issuing one of the five writs as per the case**. 
 
• The Supreme Court is considered as the protector and guarantor of the fundamental rights(Article 32). 

 
 

 __Article__
 __Detail__
 
 

 **Article 226**
 
 
**States about the Power of high court to issue certain writs.**

 
 
 

 Article 227
 
 
States about the Power of superintendence over all courts by the high court.

 
 
 

 Article 228
 
 
States about the Transfer of certain cases to the high court.

 
 
 

 Article 230
 
 
States about the Extension of jurisdiction of the high court to union territories.

 
 
 

 Article 231
 States about the Establishment of a common high court for two or more states.
 
 

 Article 233
 States about the Appointment of the district judge.

questions.question: In Paramecium, the food is moved to a specific spot by the movement of ________ which cover the entire surface of the cell.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Cilia.**

__**Explanation:**__

Paramecium is a genus of unicellular ciliates, commonly studied as a representative of the ciliate group.

A paramecium has thousands of cilia that rhythmically move, providing a way for the food to move around and transfer the food in the oral cavity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0b3b4de4d83ed5c20c12e2ce7d0beb3bd2fcd0acb700e5333cdb9f5ce1c9ffe8.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**There are different types of protozoans: ameboid, ciliated, flagellated, and sporozoan.

 
• Ameboid protozoans

 
 
• They are found in moist soil and freshwater/ seawater.
 
• They capture their prey by putting out pseudopodia also called false feet.
 
• An example is *Amoeba.*
 
• *Amoeba* also has a contractile vacuole, it is an osmoregulatory organ.
 
• The contractile vacuole controls the intracellular water balance by expelling excess water from the body.
 
 
 
• Flagellated protozoans
 
 
• They have flagella as a locomotory organ.
 
• They can be free-living or parasitic.
 
• An example is *Trypanosoma*. It causes sleeping sickness.
 
 
 
• Ciliated protozoans
 
 
• They are aquatic and actively moving organisms because of the presence of locomotory organs called cilia.
 
• The cilia help in the movement of water along with the food inside the body cavity.
 
• An example is *Paramoecium*. It has a dimorphic nucleus.
 
• It has one small nucleus called a micronucleus and one large nucleus called a macronucleus.
 
 
 
• Sporozoans
 
 
• They have an infectious spore-like stage in their life cycle.
 
• An example is* Plasmodium*. It causes malaria in humans.

questions.question: Which among the following is respiratory pigment in human beings?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Haemoglobin.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The Hemoglobin molecules with the help of external chemical factors take up oxygen molecules in the lungs and then send them to the various tissues of our body.

 
• Iron is the **main constituent** of hemoglobin.
 
• The **normal level** of hemoglobin is 13 to 17 grams per deciliter in men and 12.0 to 15.5 grams per deciliter in women.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• Melanin is a dark biological pigment found in skin, hair, feathers, scales, eyes, and some internal membranes.
 
• Rhodopsin is called visual purple, a pigment-containing sensory protein that converts light into an electrical signal. 
 
• **Bilirubin** is a yellowish substance in your blood. It **forms after red blood cells break down**, and it travels through your liver, gallbladder, and digestive tract before being excreted.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The biggest regulator of oxygen affinity in Hemoglobin is the oxygen itself.
 
• If in the lungs, the oxygen levels are high the Hemoglobin shows a greater affinity towards the oxygen molecules, and as it bounds to more oxygen, this property of affinity increases and vice versa.
 
• When the Oxyhemoglobin binds to the maximum capacity, it becomes saturated but its affinity towards oxygen increases whereas when this binding loose oxygen molecule the affinity decreases.
 
• This regulation activity is called Cooperativity and is an important function as it allows the maximum amount of Hemoglobin to be carried to the tissues and also allows deoxyhemoglobin which is releasing the oxygen tissue.

questions.question: In May 2017, the base year of All-Indian WPI (Wholesale Price Index) has been revised from 2004-05 to_________.
questions.solution:
The Wholesale Price Index (WPI) is the price of a representative basket of wholesale goods.

India has adopted new Consumer price Index to measure inflation since it considers the price at which the final consumer purchases essential consumer goods.

questions.question: From May 2017, the Real estate act has come into effect. It aims to protect the interests of _________.
questions.solution:
The Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 is an Act of the Parliament of India which seeks to protect home-buyers as well as help boost investments in the real estate industry.

The Act establishes Real Estate Regulatory Authority (RERA) in each state for regulation of the real estate sector and also acts as an adjudicating body for speedy dispute redressal.

questions.question: Calculate the frequency (in Hz) of a sound wave of wavelength 4m travelling with a speed of 200 m/s.
questions.solution: The hertz (symbol: Hz) is the derived unit of frequency in the International System of Units (SI) and is defined as one cycle per second. The wavelength is the spatial period of a periodic wave which is basically the distance over which the wave's shape repeats. It is thus the inverse of the spatial frequency.

questions.question: The numerical value of a physical quantity is its ________.
questions.solution:
An order of magnitude is an approximate measure of the size of a number, equal to the logarithm rounded to a whole number.

For example, the order of magnitude of 1500 is 3, because 1500 = 1.5 × 10³

questions.question: Humidity is a measure of the ________.
questions.solution:
• Humidity is the amount of water vapour present in the air. Water vapour is the gaseous state of water and is invisible to the human eye.
 
• Humidity indicates the likelihood of precipitation, dew, or fog.
